catalog_floods.method: each Tier B flood day (events/flood_days.json) matched to the site; strength is the strongest of name > near > area; catalog days are reported floods, so a year with no report is not proof of no flood

rules.area: an area with confidence neighbourhood or area within 1,500 m; fallback geocodes (geocoded_from set) count as area at best
rules.name: a hand-checked place token (PLACE_TOKENS in pipeline/build_sites.py) appears in a day's area name, compared with case, hyphens, spaces and punctuation removed
rules.near: an area with confidence exact or street (not a fallback geocode) within flood_radius_m + 200 m of the site geometry
rules.never: confidence city, lga or unknown, and un-geocoded areas, never match
rules.riverine_days: matched days whose flood_type is riverine
rules.sources: up to 3 of the day's reports naming a matched area, else the first reports; url, publisher, quote
rules.years_searched: years with an April-November entry in flood_days.json meta.search_coverage (not the live search log)

notes: Deterministic: sorted keys and lists, no timestamps; identical inputs give identical bytes.

Reviewer fields (verdict, change.summary) are carried from the previous events/sites.json by site_id; verdict.stale / change.stale flag a run whose underlying numbers changed. stale stays true until the reviewer clears it and the numbers hold steady.
meta.citywide_cause_statements are citywide and are never attached to a site.
Wayback detail chips inherit their acquisition's resolution_m (crops of the same image); the app hides coarse fallbacks (e.g. 15 m).
When events/promises.json appears (Task 22), re-run this script to fill promise_ids.

rules.buildings_match: baseline segments whose 2016 20–50 m built fraction is within ±max(0.05, 0.5 × the site's); matched_pct = percent of matched segments whose 2016→2023 0–10 m change is below the site's
rules.claims: the site's evidence_ids plus matched features with human causes; evidence_status parsed from the event dossier's Cause (preliminary) section
rules.floods: per event, evidence features within flood_radius_m of the site geometry (400 m; 600 m for LineStrings longer than 2 km), excluding location_confidence 'lga'; includes events other than the site's own
rules.human_causes: all cause tags except: canal_overflow, heavy_rain, lagoon_tide, low_lying_terrain
rules.s2_wet_season: per-year median of May–Oct monthly vegfrac for the recorded AOI (step-detector output not used)

verdict.text: A resident blamed the AFA bridge works for worsening the Aug 2025 flood. The works were real and long-running (awarded about 2018; the new elevated deck was still unfinished in Aug 2025), and imagery shows the corridor and earthworks in place by Apr 2025. But nothing shows them blocking the Afa river: no coffer dam is named, a reporter on 5 Aug 2025 saw the old low bridge overtopped and excavators failing to divert the water, and no official answered the claim. The crossing flooded in the rain before the works too (canoes, 2024). The inbound deck opened on 8 Sep 2026; no later flood or imagery yet.

verdict.text: The Environment Commissioner said in 2024 that Agungi's road collector was too small and that development had outgrown the drainage, but no size or build date was ever published, so the claim can't be measured. Building within 10 m of the road corridor rose from 0.9% (2016) to 3.4% (2023), above 71% of comparable channels, and imagery shows infill and a new estate at the lagoon end: consistent with the claim, not proof of it. The promised new collector is not documented as started, and imagery stops at Nov 2024. Agungi flooded again in Sep 2025, and by Jun 2026 the state was blaming a blocked Ajiran outfall instead, while saying unnamed 'major drainage' had been finished.

sites.located_how: Official texts place System 156 upstream on Alpha Beach Road, with excavation 'from Alpha Beach to conservation road' and a blockage 'along Alfa Beach behind James Hope University'. OSM has no name 'System 156' or 'Alpha Beach Road'. Overpass returns a continuous unnamed drain/ditch at ~3.511°E from ~6.427–6.444°N, west of Lekki Conservation Centre (OSM ~3.535, 6.443) and of the evidence neighbourhood point (3.515, 6.430). Line is that mapped drain (OSM ways 599933032 + 295026376).
sites.name: Alpha Beach – System 156

verdict.text: Officials blamed developers for blocking System 156, and three independent records agree. Sentinel-2 shows the land beside the channel's south end losing most of its vegetation in 2021–22. Google Open Buildings shows building within 10 m of the channel rising from 3.6% (2016) to 9.4% (2023), mostly 2019–22, more than 88% of comparable city channels. Wayback imagery shows wetland and informal settlement cleared and sand-filled. All of it predates the July 2024 flood and the state's June 2024 excavation.

Guardian/Vanguard 27 Oct 2022 place the viral-flood reach "behind Abimbola Awoniyi Estate by Agric Road, Oko Oba, Agege". Maps: Abimbola Awoliyi Estate 3.31209, 6.64853 (Ifako-Ijaiye/Ojokoro). OSM Agric Road (ways 586770836, 4992769) runs east of the estate; way 586770837 is a 15 m bridge on Agric Road at 3.31474, 6.64940, and way 586763553 is a bridge on Akinsegun Street at 3.31552, 6.65149 — the only mapped crossings that can carry the channel. Line is those two bridges extended ~150 m along the same bearing (not Oko Oba Road, which Task 18 imagery showed was the previous line). Canal centreline itself remains unlabelled. | 2026-10-17 (reviewer): channel traced by hand on current Esri World Imagery (z18): an open vegetated channel running S→N from the Agric Road bridge (3.31474, 6.64940) past Abimbola Awoniyi Estate; Task 19 line followed it in the south but veered NE onto streets in the north.

verdict.text: The canal overflowed on 9 Jul 2022 while the state says it was being expanded. On imagery it is a narrow, overgrown open channel with buildings close on both banks: about 13% of the land within 10 m was already built by 2016, unchanged since. That is long-standing encroachment rather than new building, consistent with the state's Oct 2022 'infringed channel' notices. The promised 8 m widening and removal of structures aren't visible by May 2025.
